test_cases.name: WEAR-001 | Activate a customer's own watch as a paired line on their phone
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
BYOW (Bring Your Own Watch) lets a rep add a customer-owned smartwatch to the account as a paired line on an existing phone. The watch has no physical SIM — it is provisioned via its 32-digit EID (eSIM) — and its plan is paired to a voice line the rep explicitly selects. A watch can never be line 1: a primary phone line must exist first.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2012 (Epic: Wearable Activations), RTPL-2347 (pairing/standalone plan), RTPL-2576 (watch eSIM-only), RTPL-2205 (watch compatibility)

## Preconditions
- ConfigCat flags enable_subscriber_activation_byod = ON and enable_subscriber_activation_watch = ON.
- A primary phone line already activated/added on the order (rule 9 — watch cannot be line 1), then add-line for the watch.
- New account created + ID verified (as in the handset happy path).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Watch IMEI:** Real customer-owned BYOW watch IMEI (family 36040; Apple then Samsung for pairwise). Single-IMEI, byodType 'W'
- **EID:** Valid 32-digit numeric ^[0-9]{32}$ (watch is eSIM-only — no physical SIM)

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Watch is eSIM-only — assert the EID screen appears and NO pSIM card (RTPL-2576).
- Pairing MDN is rep-selected, never auto-picked (RTPL-2347).
- Blocked to AR-2 until a real watch IMEI + valid EID are provisioned (workbook EID column float-corrupted).

steps.action: On the added line (line 2), rep enters the watch IMEI
steps.expected: [BE] POST validate-device -> deviceType='WEARABLE', byodType='W', isByod=true, countOfSims=1, imei2=null. [FE] 'IMEI not found' drawer (customer-owned)

steps.action: Rep clicks Continue in the drawer, then picks the watch device type
steps.expected: [Both] accept-add-as-byod; [BE] availableByodDeviceTypes = watch codes only (no handset codes); [FE] watch type selected, Continue enabled

steps.action: Rep clicks Continue
steps.expected: [BE] selectedByodDeviceType = the watch code; simOptions[0].simType='ESIM'. [FE] EID entry screen (NOT a physical-SIM card) — RTPL-2576

steps.action: Rep enters the 32-digit EID and Continues
steps.expected: [Both] provide-eid accepted; deviceValidationDetails.eid set; flow advances to number/plan

steps.action: Rep reaches plan selection and picks a paired watch plan
steps.expected: [BE] GET selection-options/plans; [FE] paired plan selected; a pairing-MDN selector appears (paired SOC requires a pairing line)

steps.action: Rep selects the pairing MDN (the phone line) and Continues
steps.expected: [Both] configure-plan with selectedPairingMdn set; [BE] primarySubscriberForPairing recorded; no pairing-mdn-required error

steps.action: Rep completes promotions(skip) -> add-ons(skip) -> Create subscriber
steps.expected: [BE] watch line activated (deviceInfoSource = watch code); no error 100000004/999999963

steps.action: Rep completes Order Summary -> Add Accessory (none) -> cash payment (exact)
steps.expected: [Both] Order Summary 'Lines in order: 2'; [BE] collect-cash -> collect-payment; SaleRecord persists (no TEMP-) with BOTH lines and the watch Device row at $0.00

test_cases.name: WEAR-002 | Offer only watch device types when registering a customer's watch
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
When a rep registers a customer-owned watch, the device-type picker must offer watch types only (never handset/tablet). A regression once resolved Samsung/Apple watch IMEIs as phones and showed phone options — corrupting the whole activation.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2557 (watch IMEIs misidentified as phones), RTPL-2205

## Preconditions
- BYOW flow entered via accept-add-as-byod on a watch IMEI (primary phone line already present).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Watch IMEI:** Real BYOW watch IMEI (Apple + Samsung, family 36040)

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Two-layer: intercept availableByodDeviceTypes AND assert rendered DOM. Assert by code, not i18n label.
- RTPL-2557 regression signal: a watch IMEI that surfaces handset options is a fail.

steps.action: Rep reaches the device-type picker after accepting the watch as BYOD
steps.expected: [FE] required radio group shown

steps.action: Rep reads the offered options
steps.expected: [Both] rendered options = watch types only (BYOW-APPLEWATCH, BYOW-SAM); [BE] availableByodDeviceTypes contains NO handset/tablet codes (no BYOD-ANDROID/IPHONE/BYOT)

steps.action: Rep confirms a Samsung and an Apple watch IMEI both resolve to watch (RTPL-2557)
steps.expected: [BE] isWatch=true / deviceType='WEARABLE' for both — never phone options

test_cases.name: WEAR-003 | Reject a phone device type applied to a customer's watch
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
The device-type picker must be trustworthy end-to-end: a handset code (e.g. BYOD-ANDROID) must never be accepted for a watch IMEI. The backend must reject the mismatched code rather than silently flipping the line to a phone (a past bug returned 200 OK and overwrote isWatch true->false).

## Related tickets
RTPL-2556 (cross-device guard — code accepted for wrong class, isWatch overwritten)

## Preconditions
- BYOW flow: watch IMEI validated and accepted as BYOD (isWatch=true).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Watch IMEI:** Real BYOW watch IMEI (family 36040)
- **Invalid device-type code (API bypass):** BYOD-ANDROID (handset-only)

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- API layer is the real guard (RTPL-2556 was a 200 OK + isWatch flip). Assert on re-read state, not just the click response.

steps.action: Rep validates the watch IMEI and accepts BYOD
steps.expected: [BE] isWatch=true

steps.action: Rep views the picker
steps.expected: [FE] BYOD-ANDROID is not offered / not selectable

steps.action: (API bypass) submit select-byod-device-type with deviceType:'BYOD-ANDROID'
steps.expected: [BE] HTTP 400 invalid-byod-device-type — mismatched code rejected

steps.action: Re-read line state
steps.expected: [BE] isWatch still true (NOT overwritten); selectedByodDeviceType unchanged

test_cases.name: WEAR-004 | Provision a customer's watch by eSIM/EID, never a physical SIM
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
A smartwatch has no physical SIM — it must be provisioned via its 32-digit EID. RTGO must show the EID entry screen (never a physical-SIM card) for a watch, accept a valid 32-digit EID, and reject wrong lengths/charsets. A bug once presented a physical-SIM step for watches.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2576 (watch presented physical SIM instead of eSIM/EID), RTPL-2414 (missing-eid)

## Preconditions
- BYOW flow at the SIM/EID step for a watch line (primary phone line present).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Watch IMEI:** eSIM watch IMEI (family 36040, variant 1 = eSIM)
- **EID (valid):** 32-digit numeric ^[0-9]{32}$
- **EID (invalid, BVA):** 31 digits; 33 digits; 32 chars incl. a letter

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Decisive assert: the SIM step for a watch is the EID screen, and no pSIM line ever appears in cart/SaleRecord.
- BVA as one parameterized spec: [31, 32, 33, 32+alpha].

steps.action: Rep reaches the SIM/EID step for the watch
steps.expected: [FE] EID entry screen shown — NO physical-SIM card offered (RTPL-2576); [BE] simOptions[0].simType='ESIM'

steps.action: Rep enters a 31-digit, then 33-digit, then 32+letter EID
steps.expected: [FE] each rejected by ^[0-9]{32}$; flow does NOT advance

steps.action: Rep enters a valid 32-digit EID and Continues
steps.expected: [Both] provide-eid accepted; deviceValidationDetails.eid set; flow advances

steps.action: Rep completes plan -> pairing MDN -> activate -> Order Summary -> Add Accessory -> cash payment
steps.expected: [BE] watch provisioned via eSIM; NO physical SIM line in the SaleRecord; SaleRecord persists (real number)

test_cases.name: WEAR-005 | Require the rep to choose a pairing line for a paired watch plan
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
A paired watch plan (Paired SOC) shares a phone line's service, so the rep must explicitly choose which voice line to pair to. RTGO must block finishing the watch line on a paired plan until a pairing MDN is selected — it must never silently auto-pick or proceed without one.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2347 (smartwatch pairing + standalone plan selection), RTPL-2012

## Preconditions
- BYOW watch line at plan selection; account has at least one eligible voice line (availableSubscriberForPairing non-empty).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Watch IMEI:** eSIM BYOW watch IMEI
- **Plan:** A paired watch SOC (e.g. AWATCHPR / FAMWATCH) — discovered at run time

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Candidate lines come from BE availableSubscriberForPairing; the rep's pick is submitted as selectedPairingMdn — never auto-picked (RTPL-2347).
- Assert by SOC class (paired vs standalone), not price.

steps.action: Rep selects a paired watch plan and tries to continue WITHOUT choosing a pairing MDN
steps.expected: [Both] 400 pairing-mdn-required; flow stays at plan/pairing; [FE] pairing-MDN selector flagged required

steps.action: Rep selects a pairing MDN from the offered voice lines and continues
steps.expected: [Both] accepted; selectedPairingMdn / primarySubscriberForPairing set; flow advances to promotions

test_cases.name: WEAR-006 | Reject an invalid or unavailable pairing line for a watch
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
When pairing a watch, the chosen pairing MDN must be one of the account's eligible voice lines. Submitting a number not in the offered list must be rejected; and if the account has no voice line to pair with at all, the paired plan cannot proceed.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2347 (pairing-mdn-invalid / pairing-mdn-unavailable)

## Preconditions
- BYOW watch line at the pairing-MDN step.

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Watch IMEI:** eSIM BYOW watch IMEI
- **Invalid pairing MDN:** A number NOT in availableSubscriberForPairing

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Two rules from RTPL-2347: invalid (not in list) vs unavailable (none exist). Assert the exact reason code per branch.

steps.action: Rep submits a pairing MDN that is not in the offered list
steps.expected: [Both] 400 pairing-mdn-invalid; flow does NOT advance

steps.action: (No-voice-line account) Rep reaches a paired plan with no eligible voice line
steps.expected: [Both] pairing-mdn-unavailable — paired plan cannot be completed; rep must pick a standalone plan or add a voice line

test_cases.name: WEAR-007 | Suppress pairing for a standalone watch plan
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
A standalone watch plan (Standalone SOC) does not pair to a phone line, so RTGO must auto-suppress the pairing-MDN selector for it — and defensively reject any pairing MDN submitted with a standalone plan.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2347 (standalone plan selection; standalone-pairing-not-allowed)

## Preconditions
- BYOW watch line at plan selection with a standalone watch SOC available.

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Watch IMEI:** eSIM BYOW watch IMEI
- **Plan:** A standalone watch SOC (e.g. AWATCHSA / WATCHSA) — discovered at run time

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Assert the message/copy matches approved i18n (RTPL-2347 AC: 'Unpaired plan selected — voice line pairing unavailable.' — confirm exact copy before pinning).
- Standalone SOC set = UNPAIRED_WATCH_SOC_CODES; assert by socCode.

steps.action: Rep selects a standalone watch plan
steps.expected: [FE] no pairing-MDN selector shown (pairing suppressed); flow can proceed without a pairing MDN

steps.action: (Defensive, API) submit a standalone plan WITH a non-null pairing MDN
steps.expected: [BE] 400 standalone-pairing-not-allowed

test_cases.name: WEAR-008 | Block an incompatible watch before it enters BYOD
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
Not every customer-owned watch can join the network. Metro runs a compatibility pre-check; a watch that is not 'Available to Activate' must be blocked before the BYOD flow starts, with a clear reason — never silently advanced.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2205 (watch compatibility pre-check; watch-not-compatible-for-byod)

## Preconditions
- Watch IMEI that Metro flags as not compatible for BYOD.

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Incompatible watch IMEI:** A watch IMEI Metro returns as not compatible

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- The FE 'verify watch compatibility' landslide screen was resolved Won't-Do (RTPL-2016); only the BE pre-check remains — assert the reason code, not a dedicated screen.

steps.action: Rep enters the incompatible watch IMEI
steps.expected: [Both] reason code watch-not-compatible-for-byod; [FE] block message shown

steps.action: Rep confirms no BYOD entry occurs
steps.expected: [BE] no accept-add-as-byod path, no device-type picker, line does not advance

test_cases.name: WEAR-009 | Bill and save both lines when a phone and paired watch are on one order
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
A customer can activate a phone and a paired watch on one order. Both lines must be itemized on the invoice AND persisted in the SaleRecord — an earlier bug silently dropped the watch line from the SaleRecord though full payment was taken, breaking reconciliation. This proves nothing is dropped.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2641 (watch line dropped from receipt/SaleRecord — Verified), RTPL-2297 (activation failed for multi-line wearable)

## Preconditions
- enable_subscriber_activation_byod = ON and enable_subscriber_activation_watch = ON.
- Line 1 = phone (BYOD or A-Stock) activated; watch added as line 2 via add-line (rule 9).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Line 1 IMEI:** Phone IMEI (BYOD handset or A-Stock)
- **Line 2 Watch IMEI:** Real BYOW watch IMEI (Apple, then Samsung for pairwise)
- **Line 2 EID:** Valid 32-digit EID

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Decisive oracle = SaleRecord item COUNT (must be 2), not invoice rendering (RTPL-2641).
- A watch line resolving to ZERO sale items must fail loudly/alert, never persist silently.

steps.action: Rep activates line 1 (phone) through activate-subscriber
steps.expected: [BE] phone line activated

steps.action: Rep Add-a-line, enters the watch IMEI -> accept BYOD -> watch type -> EID -> paired plan + pairing MDN -> activate
steps.expected: [BE] watch line activated; [Both] watch line cart HAS a 'Device' row at $0.00 (a missing Device row is the drop precursor)

steps.action: Rep reviews Order Summary
steps.expected: [Both] 'Lines in order: 2'; both LINE ONLY ACTIVATION

steps.action: Rep completes Add Accessory -> cash payment (exact)
steps.expected: [BE] SaleRecord contains EXACTLY 2 LINE ONLY ACTIVATION items + payment; watch LineState.Pricing.Device non-null; QPAY total matches Order Summary

steps.action: Repeat with a Samsung watch as line 2 (pairwise)
steps.expected: [BE] same integrity

test_cases.name: WEAR-010 | Prevent a watch from being the first line on an order
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
A watch is an accessory line — it cannot be activated on its own as line 1; a primary phone line must exist first. Starting an order with a watch as the first line must be prevented so the pairing/plan model stays valid.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2012, Section-0 rule 9 (tablet/watch cannot be line 1)

## Preconditions
- Fresh order with no activated primary line.

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Watch IMEI:** BYOW watch IMEI (family 36040)

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Guard mirrors the tablet line-1 rule. Assert the watch-first path is blocked and the add-line-second path works.

steps.action: On a brand-new order (no primary line), rep enters the watch IMEI as line 1
steps.expected: [Both] the flow does NOT allow the watch as line 1 — rep is required to add/activate a primary phone line first

steps.action: Rep adds a primary phone line, then adds the watch as line 2
steps.expected: [Both] watch now accepted on line 2; flow proceeds normally
